Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 2 to 3 months. No known injury.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Moderate leaking multilobulated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear with dominant radial component at the posterior root. Severe meniscal extrusion. No displaced meniscal flap or fragment.
Medial compartment cartilage: Confluent regions of high-grade articular cartilage loss at both sides of the weightbearing aspect of the joint, including some areas of full-thickness fissuring and associated subchondral signal changes. High-grade cartilage loss at the posterior medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity and high-grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint with regions of full-thickness fissuring and associated subchondral signal changes.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage loss at the patella, including areas of full-thickness cartilage loss at the median ridge, medial patellar facet, and lateral patellar facet. Full-thickness chondral fissuring at the medial and lateral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear. Small intrasubstance ganglion formation at the tibial insertion.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 11 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Complex tear of the medial meniscus with dominant radial component at the posterior root. Severe meniscal extrusion.
2.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, worst at the medial tibiofemoral component, where it is severe. Small knee joint effusion. Moderate leaking multilobulated Baker's cyst.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Tendinitis rotuliana. Obs. Edema óseo, tuberosidad anterior de la tibia.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones.
Úlcera condral focal de espesor total de la faceta medial de la rótula, sin cambios óseos
secundarios. Aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Leve aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la inserción proximal del
tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Discreto edema de las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Edema del tejido celular subcutáneo del aspecto anterior de la rodilla, adyacente a la tuberosidad
anterior de la tibia, sin colecciones líquidas regionales.
Impresión:
Condropatía focal grado 3 de la faceta medial de la rótula.
Signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de la rótula.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal y rotuliana proximal.
Fenómenos de fricción de la banda iliotibial, correlacionar con clínica.
Edema del tejido celular subcutáneo del aspecto anterior de la tibia adyacente a la tuberosidad
anterior de la tibia, sin colecciones líquidas regionales

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Condropatía troclear derecho.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.

SAĞ DİZ  MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Medial menisküste grade III dejenerasyon ve horizontal yırtığı izlendi. Medial menisküs mediale doğru ekstrude görünümdedir. Medial kollateral ligamen çevresinde periligamentöz ödem ile uyumlu görünüm mevcuttur ( grade I sprain ). Lateral menisküste grade II dejenerasyon izlendi. Ön çapraz bağda miksoid dejenerasyon ile uyumlu sinyal artışı mevcuttur.Arka çapraz bağ proksimal düzeyde kalınlaşma ve sinyal artışı izlendi. Meniskofemoral ligamanda belirgin kalinlaşma ve sinyal artişi izlendi.Patella normal yerleşimlidir. Retinakulumlar normaldir. Patellar tendon normaldir.Diz eklemini oluşturan kemik yapılarda hafif osteofitik sivrileşmeler ve tibiofemoral eklem medialde eklem mesafesinde hafif daralma ve komşu kartilajlarda hafif incelmeler izlendi ( dejeneratif artrit bulguları ).  Tibia interkondiler tüberkül ACL yapışma düzeyinde subkondrial milimetrik kistler izlendi.Diz eklemi içerisinde hafif sıvı artışı izlendi. Gastrocnemius medial krus femoral yapışma düzeyinde parsiyel yırtık ile uyumlu görünümler ve bu alanda kistik görünüm mevcuttur. Popliteal fossada yaklaşık 16 mm çapta baker kisti izlendi.

Interprétation : 

Il y a un minime liséré de liquide au sein du récessus suprapatellaire, sans épanchement intra-articulaire significatif. Il y a un petit kyste de Baker, sans complication significative, mesurant 2,8 cm de diamètre CC.

Il y a une déchirure longitudinale horizontale impliquant la corne postérieure et le corps du ménisque interne, s’étendant à la racine postérieure, à la jonction avec la corne antérieure et le long de la surface articulaire inférieure. Il y a de petits kystes paraméniscaux associés au versant postérieur. 

Il y a un épaississement des fibres superficielles du ligament collatéral interne avec un œdème léger à modéré au pourtour suggérant une entorse de grade 1. 

Il y a une atténuation légère à modérée des surfaces chondrales au compartiment fémorotibial interne , sans atteinte transfixiante. Il y a de petits ostéophytes marginaux. 

Le ménisque externe et le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe sont intacts et sans déchirure.

Il y a une légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces chondrales au compartiment fémorotibial externe avec un foyer de chondropathie sévère à la surface non-portante au versant postérieur du condyle fémoral externe avec une perte focale transfixiante de la surface cartilagineuse et un début de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Il y a de minimes ostéophytes marginaux.

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts et sans déchirure. Il y a de minimes kyste ganglionnaires intra-osseux sous l’insertion distale du ligament croisé antérieur. 

L’alignement patellofémoral parait dans les limites de la normale. Il y a plusieurs artéfacts de susceptibilité magnétique au versant antérieur du tendon patellaire, le plus probablement de nature post-interventionnel/chirurgical; à corréler cliniquement. 

Les tendons du quadriceps distal et patellaire sont grossièrement intacts et sans déchirure. 

Il y a un léger épaississement prépatellaire qui pourrait être en lien avec des séquelles de bursite.

Il y a une légère atténuation des surfaces chondrales au compartiment patellofémoral, principalement à la surface trochléaire avec des foyers de chondropathie sévère le long de l’échancrure intercondylienne et de la facette trochléaire externe avec fissures transfixiantes et des changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Il y a de petits ostéophytes marginaux. 

Il y a des microkystes ganglionnaires millimétriques en lien avec l’articulation tibiofibulaire proximale.

Conclusion :

Déchirure longitudinale horizontale de la corne postérieure et du corps du ménisque interne telle que décrite ci-haut avec de petits kystes paraméniscaux associés au versant postérieur.

Entorse de grade 1 du ligament collatéral interne. 

Changements dégénératifs/chondropathie tricompartimentale avec des foyers de chondropathie sévère à la surface non-portante au versant postérieur du condyle fémoral externe et le long de la surface trochléaire au compartiment patellofémoral. 

Pas d'épanchement intra-articulaire significatif.

Petit kyste de Baker non-compliqué.

Autres trouvailles telles que décrites ci-haut.

Findings:  There is a mild - moderate knee effusion. There is incomplete tearing of the posterior root of the medial meniscus. The medial meniscus is partly extruded from the joint. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild - moderate thinning of the medial compartment articular cartilage with associated mild osteophyte formation and mild marrow edema in the weightbearing aspect of the medial tibial condyle. Minor patchy fraying of the lateral compartment articular cartilage is also noted. Mild - moderate patellofemoral degenerate changes also seen.  
Conclusion: Degenerate changes as described. Incomplete tearing of the posterior root of the medial meniscus.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. There is low grade sprain of the medial patellofemoral ligament.   
 In the intercondylar notch, the anterior posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. There is no tibial translation. 
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Some amount of right knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is bone contusion at medial femoral condyle.  
 Subcutaneous fat contusion at the anterior aspect of right knee.  Some amount of right knee effusion. 
  Bone contusion at medial femoral condyle.  
  Low grade sprain of the medial patellofemoral ligament.   
  Subcutaneous fat contusion at the anterior aspect of right knee.

Moderate suprapatellar effusion, there are no intra-articular bodies.
Both menisci appear intact, as do the cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus musculotendinous unit, distal iliotibial band and extensor tendons.
Well-maintained tricompartmental hyaline articular cartilage surfaces, save for a tiny cartilage fissure present just lateral to the median patellar ridge, with similar appearances being noted at the medial facet of the distal femoral trochlea. 
No fracture or marrow infiltration.  Grossly unremarkable imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain in right knee
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst with partial rupture.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Area of full-thickness fissuring at the posterolateral tibial plateau with associated subchondral edema.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Partial thickness fissuring along the median ridge/lateral fat-sat. Intact trochlear cartilage.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Mild thickening with increased intrinsic signal, likely grade 2 sprain.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 9 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

Area of full-thickness fissuring at the posterolateral tibial plateau with associated subchondral edema.

Grade 2 sprain of the PCL.
